scenarios.title: Manage a lead in the final minute
scenarios.objective: Use the stated clock and score to weigh controlled possession against a safe reset.
scenarios.briefing: Navy leads 3–2 with one minute left. Navy attacks the Gold net. YOU owns the puck near centre; F1 is wide support, F2 is higher, and Gold pressures from both sides. The score and clock are explicit practice conditions.
cues: Navy leads 3–2 with one minute left.
F1 and F2 are visible support options.

questions.prompt: Read the freeze: what lead and clock are on the board?

options.text: Navy leads 3–2 with one minute left

questions.explanation: The briefing states a one-goal Navy lead with one minute remaining.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect the possession objective?

options.text: The lead means every forward option is wrong

questions.explanation: The score and time shape risk, while support determines whether possession can be kept.

questions.prompt: Arrange a late-possession read.

options.text: Protect or move the puck to a reachable option
Re-check whether the next lane remains safe

questions.explanation: The lead informs risk, but the actual support and pressure still decide the next action.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a position with two controlled outlets visible.
questions.explanation: This point keeps F1 and F2 in separate support relationships.

questions.prompt: F1 opens with room to retain the puck. What changes?

options.text: A controlled pass may reduce pressure while keeping possession
Force a shot because the lead is close

questions.explanation: F1 becoming reachable changes the safe-possession branch; the clock does not make one action automatic.

questions.prompt: Explain a sensible risk tradeoff without saying “never attack with a lead.”
questions.explanation: With a one-goal lead and one minute, value possession and support, but use a forward lane when it is clearly reachable and pressure leaves it available.

scenarios.title: Create a chance while trailing late
scenarios.objective: Seek a reachable attacking chance while the late deficit makes risk meaningful.
scenarios.briefing: Navy trails 2–3 with one minute left and attacks the Gold net. YOU owns the puck high right; F2 is inside, F3 is wide, and Gold 1 blocks the lane. The scene supports a time-aware branch, not a forced shot.
cues: Navy trails 2–3 with one minute left.
Gold 1 blocks the direct lane; F2 is inside.

questions.prompt: What game context is stated?
questions.explanation: The briefing states Navy trails 2–3 with one minute left.

questions.prompt: Which two considerations shape a remaining chance?

options.text: The late clock matters more than checking F2 or F3

questions.explanation: The clock changes the value of risk, while support determines whether a chance can be created.

questions.prompt: Arrange this time-aware attack read.

options.text: Scan Gold 1 and the support lanes
Use the open lane if it stays reachable
Re-check whether a shot, pass or reset fits

questions.explanation: The deficit can justify risk, but the lane still needs a real read.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward a central point angle while keeping F2 visible.
questions.explanation: This point changes the carrier line toward F2 and the net while retaining the wide option.

questions.prompt: With Gold 1 in the shot lane, which F2 change matters?

options.text: A pass to F2 if the lane is reachable
Shoot through the defender without scanning

questions.explanation: The defender movement changes the lane and F2 may now be the safer chance.

questions.prompt: What does this late deficit add to feedback beyond the phrase “get a shot”?
questions.explanation: The useful decision includes time, score, pressure, support and the reachable lane. A shot is one branch, not proof that it was the best choice.

scenarios.title: Enter the power play before setup
scenarios.objective: Use a permitted rush option while checking support and the penalty-kill shape.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the Gold net on a power play. The team instruction permits a rush entry and a shot if the lane is open. YOU carries high right; F2 is middle, F3 is wide, and Gold has a staggered shape.
cues: The power-play instruction permits a rush entry.
F2 and F3 are support options.
Gold 1 and Gold 2 shape the visible pressure.

scenarios.title: Protect the backdoor during rotation
scenarios.objective: Exchange a low defensive responsibility while keeping the backdoor lane covered.
scenarios.briefing: Gold attacks the Navy net on a penalty play. YOU is low on the left side, D1 is near the net, and Gold 1 is below the line with Gold 2 across the low slot. Gold 3 can cut inward.
cues: Gold 1 has the puck below the line.
Gold 2 is across the low slot.
YOU and D1 share a changing inside responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which attacker is across the low slot from Gold 1?

questions.prompt: Which two checks belong before exchanging low responsibility?

options.text: The puck side fixes coverage forever

questions.prompt: Arrange a coverage handoff.

options.text: Re-check the slot and net-side lane

questions.prompt: Gold 2 receives below the line and Gold 3 cuts inward. What needs updating?

questions.prompt: Which backdoor and low-slot space are you protecting, and why can the pass reach them?
questions.explanation: Describe Gold 2 across the low slot and Gold 3 cutting inward. Keep the net-side lane covered, then update if Gold moves the puck or crosses.

scenarios.title: Join the second wave after possession check
scenarios.objective: Activate into a second wave only when the carrier and defensive cover remain connected.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks the Gold net. YOU is behind the play; F1 carries through centre, F2 is wide, and F3 is high. D1 is the deeper cover. The activation is a conditional support decision.
cues: F2 and F3 offer second-wave support.

questions.prompt: Which navy player has the deeper-cover role?
questions.explanation: The briefing assigns D1 as the deeper cover while F1 carries.

questions.prompt: Which two checks support joining the attack?

options.text: D1's ability to cover behind YOU
Joining because the puck is already up ice

questions.explanation: Carrier control and cover make activation safer; distance from the puck alone is not enough.

questions.prompt: What sequence checks whether YOU should join as a second wave?

options.text: Move into a reachable second-wave lane

questions.explanation: Activation is useful only while the carrier and cover remain connected.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a second-wave lane between F1 and the high support.
questions.explanation: This point joins the attack while keeping D1 and F1 in view.

questions.prompt: F1 bobbles as Gold 3 accelerates: which role change follows?

options.text: Recover or hold the cover instead of continuing forward
Keep activating because F1 started the play

questions.explanation: The carrier and pressure changed, so preserve cover or recover before joining.

questions.prompt: How do carrier control and deeper cover separate a second wave from abandoning the play?
questions.explanation: A second wave keeps the puck carrier connected and a deeper defender able to recover. If possession or cover changes, the activation decision changes too.
